newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian health workers launch national strike.
newsitem.headline: Colombian health workers launch national strike.

text.p: An estimated 120,000 Colombian doctors, nurses and health workers went on strike on Tuesday, virtually paralysing state hospitals and health centres across the country, labour leaders said.
The strikers suspended all but emergency treatment to protest the government's failure to fulfil the terms of a wage deal reached after a nationwide stoppage by state workers in February.
They are also campaigning against plans to cut back care under the state-run social security regime, which they fear will force patients to seek private medical cover or forego treatment altogether.
A Health Ministry spokesman said there was no money to meet health workers' demands and that no talks had been scheduled to resolve the strike.

"From the point of view of a doctor the problem is the poor pay and insufficient resources. We're at a point where we still have enough money to work but who knows what will happen in the future," Oscar Bernal, surgeon at the Samaritana hospital in central Bogota, said.
Doctors at state-run hospitals currently receive about $900 per month while nurses' wages range from $300 to about $550.

Pedro Contreras, chairman of the Medical Union (ASMEDAS), told Reuters: "We're not only fighting for wages but believe the government wants to reduce public health care while the majority of Colombians do not have the means to buy (private) health care."

He said the strike had hit more than 6,500 health centres and 640 hospitals across the country. Emergency services and childbirth facilities were being maintained but routine appointments and pre-scheduled operations had been cancelled, Contreras said.

In a February deal, the government agreed to give wage hikes of about 20 percent to all state workers. State health workers should have received an additional payment to bring their pay into line with other professions.
About 1,000 health workers staged a noisy but peaceful demonstration through the streets in downtown Bogota.
Health Ministry sources said the ministry would now have to appeal to Congress for an additional budget allocation.
